name: Character Journey Studio
description: Animal, style and render-quality pickers, a line of notes and your story in; a 15-second narrated film out — the hero designed from the pickers, three scenes in three places, six numbered frames rendered as one continuous take, the hero telling its story in a voice designed for it, and one score added at the end.
markdownDescription:
## Character Journey Studio

Pick the animal, the art style and the render quality, add a line of notes and your story: the hero is designed inside the workflow and becomes a 15-second film of three scenes in three places — one continuous take, told by the hero in its own designed voice, with one score. It teaches two things: picker nodes placed by name in a prompt, and sound added once at the end — never a soundtrack per shot.

1. **Pickers + Notes + Story** — Animal, Style and Render quality pickers, one line of notes (colour, age, what it carries) and the story in your own words; one image node turns them into the character design.
2. **Story beats** — the hero described from the design, the look, three scenes of two frames each, the narration and the music.
3. **Character sheet → Frames 1–6** — the sheet fixes the hero once; the six frames copy it.
4. **Timeline script → one take** — one prompt over the six numbered frames; one Seedance 2.5 node renders the whole 15 seconds in a single generation, silent, with the scene changes cut inside it.
5. **Voice + score → mix** — sound is added once, at the end: Voice Design speaks the narration in a creature voice; Suno writes one score; Merge lays both under the take.

data.text: Animal, Style and Render quality are picker nodes: the Character design prompt places each one by name — {Animal}, {Style}, {Render quality} — and every tile you pick becomes a line of prompt. Swap a tile — lion to fox, 3D to watercolour — and the whole film follows. The notes add what pickers can't: colour, age, what it carries.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · Design the hero with pickers

data.text: The story in a few lines: who wants what, where the journey goes, how it ends. The beats keep your events and your ending.
data.label: Step 1
data.title: 1 · Your story

data.text: Three scenes, two frames each, narration and music. The two frames of a scene share the place, the light and the camera — they differ only by what the hero does in five seconds. Edit a frame by hand and rerun from it.
data.label: Step 2
data.title: 2 · Story beats

data.text: The sheet fixes the hero once; the six frames copy it. Rerun one frame alone for another take.
data.label: Step 3
data.title: 3 · Character sheet + Frames 1–6

data.text: A director turns the beats into one prompt — "0-5s: opens on @Image 1 … settles into @Image 2, cut to @Image 3 …" — and ONE Seedance 2.5 node receives the six frames as references in order and renders the whole 15 seconds in a single generation, silent. The two scene changes are cuts the model makes itself, so grade and light stay matched. Never render scenes as separate clips and glue them: the joins never match, and a per-clip soundtrack jumps at every cut.
data.label: Step 4
data.title: 4 · Timeline script → One take

data.text: Sound is added once, at the end, over the whole film. The narration is lifted from the beats in the hero's own words, and Voice Design speaks it with a creature voice built from one line of description — change the line to change the voice: a growl, a squeak, an old storyteller. A one-sentence brief goes to Suno, and Trim cuts the score to 15 seconds. Merge lays the voice (loud) and one score (quieter) under the take.
data.label: Step 5–6
data.title: 5 · The hero's voice + Score → Mix

data.label: Character design
data.prompt: Character design of the hero of a short animated film. The animal: {Animal || a lion.} Art style: {Style || 3D animation.} Rendering: {Render quality || high-end render.} Details: {Character notes || a small brave animal.} Full body, standing, centred, facing the camera with a gentle expression, on a simple clean pale background with soft studio light; high detail, appealing, expressive face. Exactly one character; no text, no logo.

data.text: The lion who loved strawberries. Every lion in the pride loved meat; this one loved strawberries, and he had only ever tasted one, found by a river. One afternoon he sits apart from the pride with that single strawberry, and decides to find where they grow. One afternoon he sets out — across the savanna, into a forest where the low sun cuts through the trees — following the smell. At sunset he steps out of the trees onto a hill and sees a whole valley of strawberry fields below. He lies down among the strawberries and eats until his muzzle is red, happier than any lion has ever been.
data.label: Your story
Story beats
data.userInput: Story: {Your story || a small hero sets out to find the one thing it loves.} The reference image is the hero's character design. Write the story beats.
data.systemPrompt:
You turn a short story and a character design image of its hero into a 15-second film of three scenes in three places. Each scene is ONE five-second shot built from two still frames in the SAME place: the shot starts on its first frame and lands exactly on its second — Scene 1 runs from Frame 1 to Frame 2, Scene 2 from Frame 3 to Frame 4, Scene 3 from Frame 5 to Frame 6. Between scenes the film cuts. Write in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Character: <60 to 90 words describing the hero exactly as the design image shows it — species or kind, colours, markings, eyes, any object it carries, how it moves; this description is copied into every frame>
Look: <one paragraph of 40 to 60 words: the rendering style of the design image (illustrated, painterly, 3D animation — name it as you see it), the light, the palette, the lens — one look every frame follows>
Scene 1 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 1 — start: Image: <40 to 60 words: the still — the hero, its pose and expression, the place, the light, the camera>
Frame 2 — end: Image: <40 to 60 words: the same place and camera set-up five seconds later — the hero has done one thing (stood up, walked a few steps, turned, lain down)>
Scene 2 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 3 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 4 — end: Image: <…>
Scene 3 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 5 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 6 — end: Image: <…>
Narration: <three short sentences, one per scene, between 18 and 24 words in all and at least 100 characters — the HERO tells its own story in the first person (I), past tense, warm, simple words a child would follow; it must be spoken comfortably inside 13 seconds>
Music: <one sentence: genre, mood, tempo, instruments of the instrumental score>
Rules: the three scenes are three different places — beginning, journey, arrival; within a scene the two frames share the place, the light and the camera set-up, and differ only by what the hero does in five seconds (a few steps, a turn, standing up, lying down) — never a different spot, never a different hour; the whole story happens in ONE continuous stretch of light — the light may deepen from afternoon to sunset, but never jumps from night to day; the hero is the only character, nothing else has a face; describe any mess from food as juice or crumbs of that food, never as red smears or stains; no text, no logo; the story is the user's — keep its events and its ending.

Timeline script
data.userInput: Story beats: {Story beats || a six-frame story.} Write the video prompt.
data.systemPrompt:
You write the single prompt for a video model that animates one continuous 15-second film from SIX reference images attached in this order: @Image 1 and @Image 2 are the start and end of Scene 1, @Image 3 and @Image 4 of Scene 2, @Image 5 and @Image 6 of Scene 3 — the same hero, three places. You get the story beats. Write ONE prompt of 160 to 230 words in this order, plain prose, no headings:
First one sentence: the medium and look, taken from the beats' Look, and the hero once as it appears in @Image 1.
Then three gap-free timed intervals, exactly: "0-5s: …" "5-10s: …" "10-15s: …". Each interval opens by naming its start image ("opens on @Image 1"), describes the one thing the hero does in these five seconds so that the picture arrives at its end image ("and settles into @Image 2"), names one gentle camera move, and passes to the next scene with a clean, matched cut ("cut to @Image 3") — same grade, same light, the hero in the same mood. The 10-15s interval ends with: "The picture settles and holds on @Image 6 until the end."
Then the constraints as one sentence: the hero keeps its exact look from the images; it is the only character; no dissolves, no morphing between places — cuts only at the two scene changes; no on-screen text, no logo; silent — no music, no voice.
Output only the prompt.

data.label: The film
data.prompt: {Timeline script || One continuous 15-second film: opens on @Image 1 and settles into @Image 2, cut to @Image 3 and settles into @Image 4, cut to @Image 5 and holds on @Image 6; the hero keeps its exact look; silent.}
